title: High-Nuclearity 3d–4f Clusters as Enhanced Magnetic Coolers and Molecular Magnets

synthesis.procedure: Cobalt(II) acetate tetrahydrate and aqueous gadolinium perchlorate were added to deionized water and anhydrous ethanol. The solution was heated to about 70 °C; freshly prepared aqueous NaOH was added dropwise with stirring to adjust the pH. After refluxing for 2 h, the solution was filtered hot. Ambient evaporation of the filtrate gave pink block-shaped crystals after two weeks.

reagents.amount: 2.0 mL of 1.0 mol L−1 solution; 2.0 mmol

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Hot filtration followed by ambient evaporation of the filtrate.

properties.summary: Exhibits a large magnetocaloric effect; magnetization did not saturate at 2 K and 7 T.

measurements.conditions: field change 7 T; lower half-maximum temperature taken as approximately 1 K

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The bowl-like Gd42Co10 core is assembled from three type-I Gd8 and three type-II Gd6Co2 units joined alternately by carbonate and hydroxide bridges, with a type-III Co4 unit in the bowl center. Three perchlorate anions occupy cup-shaped regions of the cavity (main article, Figures 1–2).

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the compound 1 procedure, substituting dysprosium perchlorate for gadolinium perchlorate: cobalt(II) acetate tetrahydrate and the lanthanide solution were combined in water and ethanol, heated to about 70 °C, adjusted with aqueous NaOH while stirring, refluxed for 2 h and filtered hot. Ambient evaporation gave pink block-shaped crystals after two weeks.

reagents.amount: 2.0 mL of 1.0 mol L−1 solution; 2.0 mmol by substitution in shared procedure

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Hot filtration followed by ambient evaporation of the filtrate.

properties.summary: Shows frequency-dependent out-of-phase ac susceptibility and slow magnetic relaxation; no out-of-phase maximum was observed under the reported zero-dc-field conditions.
